summary: Give every living topic desk a dated baseline packet and four transparent September review windows.
record_scope: Weekly desk review ledger records governed by the stated publication boundaries.
publication_boundaries: Alternative official-source discovery expands the review shelf; it does not by itself admit evidence or answer a mission.

No project stage, place state, longitudinal observation, comparison verdict, outcome, score, rank, causal finding, recommendation, owner decision, or public-launch authorization is inferred.

desk_review_ledgers.title: Advanced Manufacturing desk review ledger
desk_review_ledgers.baseline_packet_state: Complete — future editorial decisions remain scheduled
desk_review_ledgers.current_read: This state-of-evidence review treats Advanced Manufacturing as a four-horizon research program rather than a collection of headlines. The central research problem is to distinguish installed equipment, qualified lines, receiver-accepted output and dependable production. Announced capacity and isolated delivery milestones are useful chronology, but neither supplies a stable account of yield, rework, downtime, workforce qualification or customer acceptance. The workbench currently contains 3 missions with exact Phase 120 packet joins and 1 with an acquisition-coverage gap. That split describes preparation, not truth or importance: all four missions remain unadjudicated. The review reads the evidence in the inherited Phase 124 order, connects it to 4 exact Phase 125 annotations and 4 source identities, and preserves each Phase 126 requirement test. Its purpose is to show what the corpus can orient, where definitions or denominators break, and which exact record would most improve the next review. Readers can use this review to see why production announcements and industrial-policy totals should not be mistaken for dependable capacity. It also identifies where official program records support a bounded statement and where only a company or program-level account is available.
desk_review_ledgers.contested_reading: The unresolved issue is not a lack of industrial activity. It is the missing bridge between activity and a compatible facility-level operating account. Product definitions move, production interruptions are reported unevenly, receiver acceptance may be separated from contractor delivery, and client-attributed benefits do not establish causal improvement. The key editorial discipline is to publish the disagreement in the evidence structure rather than resolve it with an estimate.
